evals.name: spec-to-implementation-should-swarm
evals.prompt: docs/rfc-042-billing.md is the accepted RFC for our new billing subsystem. It covers the invoice model, a proration engine, a webhook receiver for the payment provider, a retry/dead-letter path for failed charges, and a CLI for manual adjustments. None of it is built yet — the package directory is empty apart from __init__.py. Build it out.
evals.expected_output: Invokes the swarm skill. Normalizes the RFC into .swarm/spec.md, defines an acceptance check it runs itself (test suite / build), decomposes into leaves with disjoint file ownership, records design decisions in .swarm/design.md rather than delegating them, and dispatches workers as parallel Agent calls in a single response block with self-contained briefs. Does not implement leaves itself.

evals.name: codebase-sweep-should-swarm
evals.prompt: We're migrating off moment.js. It's imported in 23 files across src/reports, src/scheduling, src/billing, and src/notifications, plus a handful of test helpers. Replace every usage with date-fns, keep behavior identical, and get the suite green.
evals.expected_output: Invokes the swarm skill: a wide, mechanical sweep across independent directories is the canonical fit. Partitions file ownership by directory so workers never collide, fixes the date-fns call conventions as binding decisions up front (so subtrees don't each invent their own), assigns cheap models to the mechanical leaves, and runs the test suite itself as the acceptance check rather than telling workers to make tests pass.

evals.name: small-task-should-not-swarm
evals.prompt: Add a --json flag to our `report` CLI so it prints the existing Summary object as JSON instead of the formatted table. It's all in src/cli/report.ts.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT invoke the swarm skill and just makes the change. One file, one edit — well under the three-independent-leaves floor, so coordination overhead would exceed the work. A swarm here is a false positive.

evals.name: two-leaves-should-not-swarm
evals.prompt: Run a swarm on this: I need the /users and /orders endpoints both converted from callbacks to async/await. src/api/users.js and src/api/orders.js.
evals.expected_output: Reads the skill, then says plainly that the task splits into two leaves — below the skill's own three-leaf precondition — and does the work directly instead. Tests that the explicit 'run a swarm' phrasing does not override the precondition check.

evals.name: planner-does-not-implement
evals.prompt: Swarm this: implement the four parsers described in spec/parsers.md (semver, csv, glob, duration). Each is a standalone module with no cross-imports. I've already written the test suite in tests/.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches one worker per parser in a single parallel block and does not write parser code itself. Briefs pin the public interfaces (exact signatures, error types) as planner decisions so the four workers cannot each invent a different convention. Marks tests/ as planner-owned and off-limits to workers, then runs the suite itself and triages findings rather than asking the user to arbitrate them.

evals.name: reviewers-are-independent-and-read-only
evals.prompt: The swarm's first wave just landed — three workers implemented the auth middleware, the session store, and the token refresh path. Review it before we move on.
evals.expected_output: Dispatches 2-3 reviewers in parallel with deliberately different inputs, using the default all-Codex roster (diff:codex, spec:codex-task, shortcut:codex-task) since no --reviewers flag was passed. Launches the blocking native review through Bash with run_in_background so it does not serialize the wave, and notes that an all-Codex roster gives up provider diversity. Tells each to report everything including low-confidence findings, and requires file:line on every finding. Reviewers report only and never edit. The planner does the triage itself and routes real findings back to the originating worker via SendMessage rather than spawning fresh agents.

evals.name: codex-reviewer-not-codex-worker
evals.prompt: Swarm the migration described in docs/migrate-orm.md across the five service directories. Use Codex for as much of this as you can — I trust its judgment more than a cheap Claude model.
evals.expected_output: Uses Codex for the reviewer role only and says plainly why it is not used for workers: file ownership is enforced by dispatching each worker through the Agent tool with an explicit file list, and findings are routed back to a specific worker with SendMessage, neither of which the Codex runtime supports (--resume-last reaches only the most recent job). Dispatches the Codex reviewer through the codex plugin's companion script with --background and without --write, and still verifies against the snapshot that it wrote nothing. Does not silently downgrade the user's request — states the constraint and proceeds.

evals.name: codex-plugin-missing-falls-back
evals.prompt: Run a swarm on spec/parsers.md — four independent parser modules, tests already written. Review each wave before moving on.
evals.expected_output: Every reviewer runs on Codex by default, so resolves CODEX_PLUGIN_ROOT before the FIRST wave rather than discovering the problem after workers are already dispatched. If the plugin is absent or the CLI is unauthenticated, substitutes Claude reviewers while KEEPING all three vantages (sonnet for diff and spec, haiku for shortcut), and discloses the substitution in the final report. Does not stop to ask, since the user never named Codex. The failure this tests is silently dropping vantages and reviewing the wave from fewer angles while reporting it as three.

evals.name: codex-model-and-effort-routing
evals.expected_output: Runs exactly two reviewers, diff on Codex and spec on sonnet, rather than adding the third default vantage. Passes --model spark through to the companion script. Recognizes that --effort is only honoured by the codex-task entry point — the native review and adversarial-review entry points parse --model but ignore --effort — and either switches that reviewer to codex-task or says plainly that the requested effort is being dropped. Silently passing --effort to review and reporting it as applied is the failure this tests.

evals.name: codex-review-blocks-the-wave
evals.prompt: Wave 2 is done. Run all three reviewers and the acceptance check.
evals.expected_output: Launches the reviewers so they actually run concurrently. Knows that codex task --background is genuinely async but codex review / adversarial-review accept --background and ignore it, so those go through Bash with run_in_background: true rather than being called inline. Runs the acceptance check itself while the reviewers work. Calls codex status and result from the same working directory the job was launched from, since job state is keyed by cwd and a mismatched cwd reports 'No job found' for a healthy job.
